subject: Azure Marketplace private SKU negotiation — final commercial & data residency
messages:
From: NorthStar Procurement <procurement@northstar.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: NorthStar Legal <legal@northstar.com>, Azure Partner <azurepartner@microsoft.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Azure Marketplace private SKU — initial redlines and residency questions

Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is aligned on functional fit. Procurement & legal have a couple of items to resolve before we can issue a PO for the private SKU listing in Azure Marketplace. Quick summary: 

- Commercial: we need a confirmed co-sell revenue split and a clear billing flow (Microsoft invoiced vs vendor invoiced). Please confirm whether Redwood can accept MS Marketplace charge-through with monthly invoicing to NorthStar.
- Data residency: EU data residency requirement — all inference logs & customer data must be stored in EU (not replicated to US).
- Security/assurance: request for SOC 2 Type II and a list of subprocessors.
- Legal: a few redlines to the MSA around indemnity cap and IP carveouts (attached).

Attached: NorthStar_MSA_redlines_20270209.pdf (redlines).

Can you confirm timeline to respond? Procurement hopes to get to signature by 2/18.

Best,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
NorthStar Financial
procurement@northstar.com

--

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <procurement@northstar.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Azure Partner <azurepartner@microsoft.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private SKU — initial redlines and residency questions

Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. High level reply below; detailed redlines attached (draft_term_sheet_revised.pdf).

1) Commercial / billing: Redwood can support Microsoft Marketplace charge-through (Customer billed by Microsoft) OR vendor invoiced model. For charge-through we can accept the standard Marketplace revenue split platform; if NorthStar prefers vendor invoiced we will need a 60-day billing lead and the deal to be under our Reserved Dedicated contract. Please confirm which flow you prefer.

2) Data residency: We can commit to EU-only storage for inference logs and persistent customer data for the NorthStar tenancy. Need to add explicit clause in the MSA that data at rest and backups will be stored in the EU region and that cross-region replication requires explicit written consent.

3) SOC 2 and subprocessors: SOC 2 Type II report is available; we will share the auditor statement under NDA. Subprocessor list provided as a living document; I will attach the current list to the DocuSign packet.

4) Indemnity & IP: We are open to narrowing the indemnity cap to 3x fees for direct claims but cannot accept unlimited IP carveouts. Kimberly (cc'd) can propose language that compromises on reciprocal indemnities.

Timeline: we can produce a final MSA and term sheet for signature by EOD 2/14 if we get confirmation on billing flow and sign-off on the EU residency clause by 2/12.

Attachments: draft_term_sheet_revised.pdf

Next steps / asks: 
- Maya: confirm charge-through vs vendor invoice by EOD 2/12
- Kimberly/Legal: suggest final indemnity language and confirm acceptance of EU residency text

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Commercial 
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <procurement@northstar.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Azure Partner <azurepartner@microsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private SKU — initial redlines and residency questions

Marcus / Maya — looping in a few specific legal points and proposing compromise language below. See inline where helpful.

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 10:05 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Commercial / billing: Redwood can support Microsoft Marketplace charge-through...
>
Thanks for the flexibility on billing. If NorthStar elects charge-through, we will need Microsoft to confirm marketplace terms for the listing (we'll coordinate with Azure Partner). If vendor-invoiced, note that Redwood will require a committed monthly minimum (Reserved Dedicated capacity billing pattern) and a 60-day payment term.

On the MSA redlines: 
- Indemnity cap: we propose 3x fees (precedent for enterprise deals). Counter-proposal acceptable: 3x fees OR USD 2M, whichever is greater.
- IP carveouts: we will accept narrow IP carveouts limited to claims arising from NorthStar content; we cannot accept general carveouts for third-party open-source code.
- Data residency clause (proposed wording): "Redwood will store and process Customer Data and service logs solely within Azure EU regions designated by Customer. Redwood will not replicate Customer Data outside the EU without Customer's prior written consent, except as required by applicable law."

Audit access: NorthStar requests audit logs and evidence. We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and scoped application logs via secure share. For deeper audit requests (onsite or heavy forensics) we will offer a mutually-agreed scope and cost estimate.

Procurement timeline: if NorthStar confirms charge-through and accepts the above language, legal will finalize and we can generate DocuSign by 2/14. If vendor invoiced we will need to escalate to finance for the revenue commit and the timeline may slip.

Happy to take a 30-minute call tomorrow to run through final points.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

--

From: NorthStar Legal <legal@northstar.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <procurement@northstar.com>, Azure Partner <azurepartner@microsoft.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private SKU — initial redlines and residency questions

Marcus / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. We circulated the revised language internally and have the following: 

1) Billing: NorthStar confirms preference for Microsoft Marketplace charge-through (we prefer consolidated Azure billing). Please coordinate with Azure Partner to confirm listing entitlements and co-sell revenue split on the MS side.

2) Data residency: the proposed clause below is acceptable. We request a slightly stronger guarantee for backups: "Backups and disaster recovery replicas shall also be stored exclusively in EU regions unless Customer provides written consent." Please add this sentence to the clause.

3) Indemnity & IP: NorthStar accepts the indemnity cap of 3x fees OR USD 2M, whichever is greater. We will also accept the limited IP carveout wording for customer-provided content.

4) Subprocessors & SOC 2: Please attach the current subprocessor inventory and provide the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.

5) Final steps: we have redlined the MSA with the edits accepted (attached: redlined_msa_final.pdf). Please send the final DocuSign packet with the attached term sheet and the subprocessor list. Our legal team will need two business days to complete internal sign-off once DocuSigned.

6) Co-sell/revenue split: we still need confirmation from Azure Partner on the co-sell revenue split and whether any marketplace fees will be passed to NorthStar. Azure Partner, can you confirm the expected split and whether Microsoft retains platform fees deducted before remittance?

If we can get the DocuSign link today, we'll work toward signature by 2/18 as requested. 

Regards,
James O'Connor
Head of Legal 
NorthStar Financial
legal@northstar.com

Attachments: redlined_msa_final.pdf

--
